lessons: Fliers carried my WG deck: two Spectral Riders, Abbey Griffin and Angel of Flight Alabaster were its finishers, so take on-colour evasion over a third ground two-drop, as the guide says.
Tonight contradicted the guide's cap on ground filler: my WG deck ran about ten ground creatures and went 2-1, though its 0-2 loss to WR shows ground-heavy lists still lose.
I had only Bonds of Faith and Spidery Grasp as flier answers, below the guide's four-answer target, so take another answer like Claustrophobia over a second Woodland Sleuth.
Tonight's UR deck won only 4 of 9 games, mostly in 15-to-22-turn stalls, so prioritise cheap creatures like Rakish Heir and Reckless Waif over top-end fliers like Moon Heron and Stitched Drake.
Round 2's WU deck also ran Claustrophobia and Sensory Deprivation, so my duplicate removal bought little against flyers; take a second early threat over a redundant removal spell.
Round 3's win came from an 18-to-22-turn grind, so Snapcaster Mage and Think Twice were worth less than a cheap threat in this slow blue-red build.
Take Stitched Drake, Voiceless Spirit and Moon Heron over a third ground body: my WU deck's fliers won the stalls, and the guide's rule to main fliers held, but Stitched Drake was not enough alone.

The guide said to hold Sensory Deprivation and Claustrophobia for fliers, but my WU deck lost 1-2 to BR-style pressure and 0-2 to the WG deck, which had Gallows Warden, Voiceless Spirit and Somberwald-style ground blockers, so count the opponent's flier answers before maining 16 lands.

Contradiction: the guide says WU with fliers and cheap removal is a good pair, yet my 2-1 to 0-2 record with 3 wins in 8 games shows that pairing alone did not hold against a WG deck with Elite Inquisitor and Bonds of Faith, so draft a bigger finisher than Silverchase Fox.
Draft more answers to fliers and pseudo-removal: my Round 3 loss to Feeling of Dread and Sensory Deprivation came with only Rebuke, Smite the Monstrous, and Into the Maw of Hell as removal.
All six of my games ran 17 to 30 turns, so my 17-land WR aggro deck needed faster pressure; prioritize two-drops and cheap evasion over expensive top-end.
White was my deepest colour and seat 6's WU went 3-0, so take white playables early and pair them with blue removal rather than cutting blue.

Contrary to the guide's skip list, tonight's BG deck (1-2) ran Darkthicket Wolf and Gruesome Deformity plus two Grizzled Outcasts beside only five evasive threats, so cap ground filler and take fliers instead.
Take a fourth flier answer over Gruesome Deformity: my deck had only Dead Weight, Tribute to Hunger and Victim of Night, the three-answer shortfall the guide warns about.
Do not discount UB: tonight's UB deck with Murder of Crows, Victim of Night and Tribute to Hunger beat my BG 2-1 despite the guide's 44%, since weak-pair averages hide strong builds.
Taking Fiend Hunter in pack 3 and Moan of the Unhallowed in pack 2 then not playing either left RG short of flyer answers against UR's Stitched Drake and Moon Heron, which cost me round 3 1-2.
Playing Garruk Relentless with three Geistflame and Ambush Viper gave me power, but my 2-drops such as Bloodcrazed Neonate lost to BG's early board, costing 0-2 in round 1.
Late picks Ghost Quarter, Memory's Journey, and the second Naturalize were dead cards; take a playable creature like Stromkirk Noble over them to fill out the curve.
Contradicts the guide's ground-filler cap: my WU deck ran about six ground bodies yet went 6-0 in games, because Grasp of Phantoms, Hysterical Blindness and Rebuke answered their threats.
Take a second Hysterical Blindness over a third ground two-drop: cheap blue removal plus Invisible Stalker and Battleground Geist won every match 2-0.
Geistcatcher's Rig is an answer to fliers, not a flier: my notes miscounted it as a finisher, so count it with removal when judging whether a deck has enough answers and evasion.

Walking Corpse, Manor Skeleton and the Markov Patrician filler gave my UB deck no clock, so the 41- and 36-turn losses to WU's Dissipate and Sensory Deprivation stalled out; prioritize evasive threats like Murder of Crows.
Against RG's Geistflame and Bloodcrazed Neonate curve, the 21-, 17- and 20-turn losses show my slow start was too late; value cheap interaction over a second Armored Skaab.
Pick removal over Disciple of Griselbrand (pick 10) and Runic Repetition (pick 13); I finished with just Victim of Night, Tribute to Hunger and two Corpse Lunge.
